payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_sigterm.py::test_a_cell_sent_sigterm_tears_down_and_closes_its_task stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'The handler is installed around `batch` too.' applied to saffron/cli.py as an edit. The claim was "`saffron cell` sent a real SIGTERM mid-IMPLEMENT, and again mid-REVIEW, returns 143 from `main`. Each time the signal raises `KeyboardInterrupt` itself, not a subclass. Its run reads `ABORTED`, its task reads `ORPHANED`, and its patch is exported to the task directory. No agent turn starts after the signal. The teardown that follows removes the critic cell's container and two volumes when REVIEW was running. It then removes the cell's own container, both its networks and both its volumes, and stops the proxy. A `KeyboardInterrupt` with no SIGTERM behind it still propagates out of `main`. In all three runs, the SIGTERM handler in place once `main` returns or raises is the one installed when `main` was called, and that handler heard nothing. While `main` runs `batch`, the SIGTERM handler is still the one in place when `main` was called.", and only that witness ran under the edit.
